summary: AI observability tools provide visibility into how LLM applications behave in production, tracking traces, latency, token usage, costs, and output quality to help teams debug failures and control spend. As LLM-powered apps scale, per-trace and per-token costs can balloon unpredictably, making observability essential for both reliability and cost management. The right tool surfaces regressions, enables evaluation of outputs, and alerts teams before problems reach users.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, token usage, latency, cost per trace, prompt/response quality, and evaluation metrics for LLM and agent workflows (tight LangChain integration).
features: Detailed tracing and debugging of chains and agents
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month with overage around $2.50 per 1,000 traces; Plus plans cited around $264 per 100,000 traces. Enterprise custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams building on LangChain/LangGraph that want deep tracing plus integrated evaluation and prompt iteration.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests via a proxy: cost, token usage, latency, request/response logs, cache hit rates, and usage by user or model.
tools.pricing: Cost-efficient at scale — approximately $79 per 100,000 traces with 30 days of data retention; free tier available for low volumes.
tools.best_for: Cost-conscious teams wanting fast, low-overhead monitoring and caching via a drop-in proxy.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: LLM traces and experiments via W&B Weave: prompt/response logs, token and cost tracking, latency, model performance, and evaluation results alongside broader ML experiment tracking.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free personal tier; team and enterprise plans are usage/seat-based with custom quotes (typically starting around $50 per seat/month for teams).
tools.best_for: ML teams already using W&B who want unified traditional ML experiment tracking plus LLM observability.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production LLM and ML performance: traces, drift, embedding/quality drift, hallucination and relevance evals, latency, token cost, and output quality at scale.
features: Open-source Arize Phoenix for local tracing
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open source; Arize AX (cloud) offers a free tier with paid Pro and Enterprise tiers at custom/usage-based pricing.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing production-grade monitoring, drift detection, and rigorous evaluation at scale.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: Traces, token usage, cost per call, latency, prompt versions, user sessions, and evaluation scores for LLM and agent applications.
features: Evaluations and scoring (manual, LLM, and custom)
tools.pricing: Open source and free to self-host; cloud Hobby tier free, Core/Pro plans starting around $29–$59/month with usage-based scaling.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, framework-agnostic observability stack with the option to self-host for data control.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token usage, latency, and costs using OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation, exportable to any observability backend.
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and frameworks
Open source with no vendor lock-in
tools.pricing: Free and open source (SDK by Traceloop); Traceloop's hosted platform offers free and paid tiers with custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Engineering teams that want standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation integrated into existing observability infrastructure.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar prompts and responses so identical requests avoid redundant API calls — proxies like Helicone make this easy.
Route tasks to the cheapest capable model: use smaller or distilled models for simple tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning.
Trim token usage by shortening prompts, compressing context, limiting max output tokens, and using prompt templates that avoid unnecessary verbosity.
Set usage monitoring, budgets, and alerts per user/feature, and batch requests where possible to catch cost spikes before they escalate.
